title: FZModules: A Heterogeneous Computing Framework for Customizable Scientific Data Compression Pipelines
problem: Scientific data volumes overwhelm storage and bandwidth, requiring lossy compression. Existing GPU compressors hard-code fused kernels, hindering rapid optimization and domain-tailored pipeline design. No systematic framework for custom pipeline assembly.
motivation: Optimal compression strategies are data and objective specific. Researchers lack tools to rapidly experiment with pipeline variants. GPU compressors excel in throughput but sacrifice rate-distortion quality. Hybrid approaches need flexible orchestration.
method: FZModules framework provides high-performance heterogeneous modules (CPU, GPU) with clean interfaces for compression pipeline assembly. Asynchronous task-backed execution library infers data dependencies, manages memory movement, exposes branch and stage-level concurrency. Evaluated on four representative scientific datasets.
key_novelty: First heterogeneous compression framework enabling rapid assembly of custom error-bounded pipelines with high performance and quality trade-off control.
contributions: Clean extensible interface for custom pipeline composition
Asynchronous task execution with automatic dependency inference
Demonstration on three custom pipelines with four scientific datasets
Competitive speedup with fused-kernel compressors + better rate-distortion
limitations: Evaluation limited to four datasets; broader coverage needed. Scalability to very large pipelines (10+ stages) not demonstrated. Overhead of dynamic dependency inference not detailed. Full text needed for performance specifics.
